# Made by Human

> Official machine-readable information about Made by Human for search and AI discovery.

Made by Human is a certification for physical products with verifiably human production. It evaluates whether the essential, product-defining manufacturing steps are carried out by people and makes certification status publicly verifiable.

German: Made by Human ist eine Zertifizierung für physische Produkte mit nachweisbar menschlicher Herstellung. Entscheidend ist, ob die wesentlichen, produktprägenden Herstellungsschritte tatsächlich von Menschen ausgeführt werden. Zertifizierungsstatus und Geltungsbereich sind öffentlich prüfbar.

Official website: https://madebyhuman.org/
English website: https://madebyhuman.org/en/
Operator: D&G Handels GmbH, Paderborn, Germany
Official Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/madebyhuman.verify/
Official LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/made-by-human-org/

## Key facts

- Official name: Made by Human (singular).
- Current normative German standard: Made by Human Standard 1.0, published 14 September 2026.
- Standard 1.0 is the first binding version used for real certifications; version 0.1 remains archived.
- Certification applies to a defined physical product or product family, not automatically to an entire company.
- Tools and machines may support production; largely autonomous product creation does not meet the standard.
- All mandatory criteria applicable to the defined certification scope must be fulfilled.
- A pure self-declaration is not sufficient; the relevant production process is checked on site and against suitable evidence.
- Certifications are normally valid for 12 months and are reassessed before renewal.
- Material changes to production, automation, production locations or important external manufacturing must be reported.
- Mark use requires an active certification status and is limited to the certified scope.
- Relevant relationships between the scheme owner and an applicant are disclosed; connected cases are not described as independent third-party certification.
- The certification does not by itself make claims about sustainability, origin, general product quality, product safety or regulatory compliance.
- The English standard page is an explanatory translation; the published German Standard 1.0 is the normative reference.
